_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: The test seeds a 12-turn conversation at /c/{{SLUG}} whose first two user messages have data-message-id {{FIRST}} and {{SECOND}}; the URL fragments that link to them are {{FIRST_FRAGMENT}} and {{SECOND_FRAGMENT}}. window.fragmentScrolls lists the data-message-id of every element scrolled into view so far, in order; check it with an eval of JSON.stringify(window.fragmentScrolls). Call "append" sends another message and waits for its reply; after it, {{APPENDED}} is the reply's data-message-id. To "set the fragment to X", eval a promise that sets location.hash to X and resolves on the next hashchange event. "At the bottom" means the messages container (".messages-container") has scrollHeight - clientHeight - scrollTop below 5 and the scroll-to-bottom button (".scroll-to-bottom-button") is hidden. To "delay" a message, rename its data-message-id attribute to data-delayed-message-id, as if its element had not mounted yet; to "mount" it, set data-message-id back from data-delayed-message-id (leaving the other attribute). Perform the steps in order. Messages arriving while a retry is pending resolve the delayed target exactly once. The page runs on a fake clock that steps drive with window.__clock. Navigate to /c/{{SLUG}} and wait for the table of contents button (".toc-button") to be visible. Pause the clock a minute from now: eval "window.__clock.pauseAt(Date.now() + 60000)". Delay message {{FIRST}}, then set the fragment to {{FIRST_FRAGMENT}}. window.fragmentScrolls must be exactly []. Mount the delayed message. Call "append", then wait for the reply to render: the paused clock delivers no animation frames, so poll an eval that advances the clock one frame and reports whether the reply is there, "(window.__clock.runFor(16), !!document.querySelector('[data-message-id=\"{{APPENDED}}\"]'))", expecting true. Then run the clock for 1100ms (eval "window.__clock.runFor(1100)"): window.fragmentScrolls must be exactly ["{{FIRST}}"].

steps.expression: new Promise(resolve => { const handler = () => { window.removeEventListener('hashchange', handler); resolve(); }; window.addEventListener('hashchange', handler); location.hash = '{{FIRST_FRAGMENT}}'; })
